Canary infos for accepted tokens come only from `on_verify_accept`, which only `run_eagle_verify` calls. The guard at config.py:981-994 checks topk and draft-token counts for any `speculative_algorithm`, so these configs pass it. Fix: in `from_env`, accept INFO with speculation only for the algorithms whose verify goes through `run_eagle_verify` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, multi-layer EAGLE, UNO), or add the hook to every other verify path.

No `canary_infos` are recorded for tokens accepted in decode, only for the prefill token from `on_sampled`. In RAISE mode `on_batch_output` raises RuntimeError inside `TokenizerManager._handle_batch_output`, which takes down the handle loop for all requests. The guard in `CanaryConfig.from_env` only asserts `speculative_eagle_topk == 1` and `speculative_num_draft_tokens == speculative_num_steps + 1`. It does not check which algorithm is in use, so these setups get past it.

The guard is config.py:84-97, not :981-994. So every decode chunk that carries spec-accepted tokens is reported as a mismatch, and in raise mode the tokenizer loop gets an exception.

🔴 With INFO enabled, multimodal, auto-truncated and session-continuation requests get false `kv_canary_info_mismatch` reports, and in RAISE mode the tokenizer's output loop crashes. The checker replays `tokenized_obj.input_ids`. The GPU side hashes `forward_batch.input_ids`, which come from the scheduler's rewritten `req.origin_input_ids`. Fix: build the checker's prompt from the same ids the scheduler writes into the canary chain, or skip requests whose ids the scheduler rewrites. This covers the multimodal-padding, truncation and session-prefix paths.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The checker is seeded at tokenizer_manager_hook.py:77 with `prompt_ids=tokenized_obj.input_ids` and hashes them at checker.py:64. The canary write kernel instead hashes `forward_batch.input_ids` (kv_canary/runner/kernel_launcher.py:76), which the scheduler builds from `req.origin_input_ids`. The scheduler rewrites those ids in three places. Multimodal pad values replace image tokens (scheduler.py:2939). Session continuation prepends a prefix (scheduler.py:2941). Auto-truncation cuts the prompt (managers/utils.py:291). In each case the GPU prefix hash differs from the CPU replay, so the first output token already mismatches. In LOG mode that is a false error on every such request. In RAISE mode, `RuntimeError` at line 64 escapes `_handle_batch_output` and kills `handle_loop`. On the base branch INFO does not exist, so these requests are unaffected.

**Verification:** The checker is seeded with `prompt_ids=tokenized_obj.input_ids` (tokenizer_manager_hook.py:74-78), but the GPU canary chain hashes `forward_batch.input_ids` from `req.origin_input_ids`, which the scheduler rewrites for multimodal padding (scheduler.py:2938-2941), session continuation and auto-truncation (managers/utils.py:291). Nothing in the hook skips these requests.

</details>

🔴 With INFO on and pipeline parallelism (`pp_size > 1`), the last PP rank's scheduler raises on its first generation step. Base canary PP runs survive this. `on_sampled` (and `on_verify_accept` at :366) attach a `CanaryInfoDeviceOutput` to `logits_output.auxiliary_device_output`. On PP, `_pp_prepare_tensor_dict` hands it to `add_auxiliary_output_to_pp_tensors`, which rejects any output that is not a `PipelineParallelAuxiliaryOutput`. Fix: reject `enable_info` with `pp_size > 1` in `CanaryConfig.from_env`, or give the canary output PP transport that does not need a sampling observer.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a server with SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1, --kv-canary log or raise, and --pp-size 2 or more. KV-canary already supports this topology; test_self_e2e_pp_baseline.py and test_self_e2e_pp_perturb.py cover it. On the last PP rank, ModelRunner.sample (model_runner.py:2217) calls on_sampled. That sets logits_output.auxiliary_device_output to a CanaryInfoDeviceOutput, which has no to_pp_tensors. scheduler_pp_mixin.py:843-848 then passes it to add_auxiliary_output_to_pp_tensors. At sampling_observer_pp.py:39-42 the isinstance check against the runtime_checkable PipelineParallelAuxiliaryOutput fails and raises RuntimeError("auxiliary output does not support pipeline-parallel transport"). The scheduler dies on the first batch. The base branch never attaches this output, so canary PP runs work there. The new config check in CanaryConfig.from_env (config.py:83-99) validates only speculative settings and never looks at pp_size.

**Verification:** Trigger: SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1, kv-canary set to log or raise, and pp_size > 1. model_runner.py:2217 calls `c.on_sampled(...)` whenever `canary_manager` is not None. sampling_observer_pp.py:39-42 then raises `RuntimeError("auxiliary output does not support pipeline-parallel transport")`. On the base branch, a canary run with PP adds no auxiliary output, so this path is never hit.

</details>

🔴 With INFO on in PD disaggregation, the decode server's scheduler crashes with AssertionError at the first decode step of every request. The base branch has no such assert, so canary PD runs work there. The decode worker adds the prefill handoff token at decode.py:2702 with no canary info. So `recorded` is empty while `commit.output_index` is 1, and `assert len(recorded) == commit.output_index` fails. Fix: reject INFO when disaggregation is on in `CanaryConfig.from_env`, or record a canary info for the handoff token on the decode side (from the prefill or recomputed) so the two lengths always match.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a PD deployment (prefill plus decode servers) with SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 and --kv-canary log or raise on the decode server. KV-canary already supports PD; pd_fixture.py, test_self_e2e_pd_baseline.py and test_self_e2e_pd_perturb.py cover it. When the transfer finishes, decode.py:2702 appends the prefill's handoff token to req.output_ids. This path skips batch-result processing, so CanaryInfoHostOutput.consume never runs for it and req.customized_info gets no canary_infos entry. On the first decode step, ModelRunner.sample calls on_sampled and produces an auxiliary output. snapshot_auxiliary_output_starts (batch_result_processor.py:227) records a start of 1. _build_auxiliary_commits then builds CommittedTokens(output_index=1, ...). consume calls setdefault(CANARY_INFOS_KEY, []), gets an empty list, and fails the assert at aux_output.py:42. The decode scheduler process dies and every in-flight request fails. The base branch adds no such output. The config check at config.py:83-99 looks only at speculative settings, not disaggregation_mode.

**Verification:** On the decode worker, decode.py:2702 adds the prefill handoff token without running batch-result processing. In aux_output.py consume, `recorded = req.customized_info.setdefault(CANARY_INFOS_KEY, [])` is empty, so `assert len(recorded) == commit.output_index` (0 != 1) raises AssertionError in the scheduler. CanaryConfig.from_env only validates the spec-decoding settings.

</details>

🟡 (optional) With INFO enabled, every `input_embeds` request fails at dispatch because the checker cannot be built from its missing or empty prompt ids. `_tokenize_one_request` forwards `obj.input_ids`, which is normally None for embeds. `len(prompt_ids)` then raises TypeError, or the explicit ValueError fires when the list is empty. Fix: have `on_request_dispatched` skip building a checker (leaving the request unchecked) when `input_ids` is None or empty. `on_batch_output` must also tolerate `state.canary_info is None` for those requests instead of asserting. [also at: python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/canary_info/tokenizer_manager_hook.py:901 - With INFO on, requests sent with `input_embeds` now fail at dispatch with a TypeError; on the base branch they are served.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

A user sends a generate request with `input_embeds` and `--disable-radix-cache`, which is the supported embeds path. tokenizer_manager.py:1128-1129 sets `input_ids = obj.input_ids`, which is None for an embeds-only request. `_send_one_request` calls `hook.on_request_dispatched` (tokenizer_manager.py:1797). That calls `_build_canary_info_checker`, and `CanaryInfoChecker.__init__` at checker.py:56 calls `len(None)`, which raises TypeError. An empty list instead raises `ValueError("kv-canary: CanaryInfoChecker requires a non-empty prompt")`. Either way the exception propagates out of `_send_one_request` before `_dispatch_to_scheduler`, so the request fails. On the base branch the same request is served normally.

🔴 With INFO on, DeepSeek-V4 servers report `kv_canary_info_mismatch` on every output chunk, and in raise mode the tokenizer output loop crashes. `_canary_info_buf` takes the first `PoolKind.FULL` group. `attach_dsv4` builds only a `PoolKind.SWA` group, so the buffer is None and `on_sampled`/`on_verify_accept` quietly emit no infos. The tokenizer hook is still active and treats the missing infos as a mismatch. Fix: make the scheduler and tokenizer agree on whether INFO is active. For example, fail at startup in `CanaryManager` or `CanaryConfig.from_env` when INFO is on and no FULL group exists, instead of silently disabling it.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a DeepSeek-V4 model (DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool) run with SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 and --kv-canary log or raise. pool_patcher/adapters/dsv4.py:33-43 returns a single CanaryBufferGroup with kind=PoolKind.SWA. canary_manager.py:74-81 therefore sets `_canary_info_buf` to None, and `_canary_info_enabled` is False. As a result no canary_infos ever go into customized_info. On the tokenizer side, CanaryInfoTokenizerManagerHook.maybe_create (tokenizer_manager_hook.py:30-36) checks only the env flag and the mode, so the hook stays active. For each non-empty chunk, `_check_canary_infos` (tokenizer_manager_hook.py:100-109) sees canary_infos None and returns a mismatch with actual=None. In LOG mode that is a false error on every chunk of every request. In RAISE mode the RuntimeError escapes `_handle_batch_output` and stops handle_loop. Without INFO the same model runs canary checks normally, and CanaryConfig.from_env (config.py:83-113) never checks the pool kind.

**Verification:** Trigger: DeepSeek-V4 with SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1. adapters/dsv4.py:33-53 returns one group with `kind=PoolKind.SWA`. canary_manager.py:74-80 looks only for a FULL group, so `_canary_info_buf` is None. CanaryConfig.from_env (config.py:84-112) never checks the pool type. `_check_canary_infos` returns a CanaryInfoMismatch whenever token_ids is non-empty. The base branch has no INFO path.

</details>

🔴 With INFO enabled, every beam-search request (`beam_width > 1`) gets a false `kv_canary_info_mismatch`. In RAISE mode it also crashes the tokenizer output loop. The dispatch guard rejects multimodal, session, input_embeds and empty prompts, but it lets beam search through. The beam leader's `output_ids` holds only `0` placeholders (coordinator.py:314, :450), so the CPU replay hashes token 0 while the GPU hashes the real beam tokens. Fix: reject `sampling_params.beam_width > 1` in this dispatch guard, the same way the other unsupported request kinds are rejected.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a generate request with `sampling_params.beam_width` set above 1, sent to a server running SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log or raise. The leader row's output is a placeholder: coordinator.py:314 runs `req.output_ids.append(0)  # length placeholder; DAG owns history` and coordinator.py:450 runs `group.leader.output_ids.append(0)`. on_batch_output then calls `checker.advance_many` with token 0 against canary infos that are either missing or computed from the real sampled tokens, so the very first chunk fails. 🔴 With INFO on, DP-attention servers using EAGLE crash the scheduler in eager verify steps, which base canary runs survive. On the eager path, `prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads `verify_forward_batch.out_cache_loc` to the DP-padded token count. `post_forward_mlp_sync_batch` never trims it back for target-verify batches. So `.view(accept_lens.numel(), num_draft_tokens)` at canary_manager.py:370 raises. Fix: take only the real rows, `out_cache_loc[: accept_lens.numel() * num_draft_tokens]`, before the view on both `run_eagle_verify` paths. Or reject DP attention in `CanaryConfig.from_env`.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log or raise, --enable-dp-attention, and EAGLE/EAGLE3. Its `out_cache_loc.view(accept_lens.numel(), num_draft_tokens)` then throws a shape RuntimeError, which kills the scheduler. 🔴 With INFO on, UNO servers log `kv_canary_info_mismatch` on every decode chunk, and in raise mode the tokenizer output loop crashes. The allow-list at config.py:92-98 admits "UNO". UNO's linear decode (`UnoWorkerV2._forward_decode`) never calls `on_verify_accept` or `on_sampled`, so only the prefill token gets a canary info. Fix: remove "UNO" from the allow-list until UNO decode emits per-token canary infos. Tree mode is already blocked by the topk==1 check.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log or raise and `--speculative-algorithm UNO --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2`. That passes the checks at config.py:92-111, and linear mode is what `_handle_uno` resolves to (speculative_hook.py:569-579). With topk 1, `tree_mode` is False (uno_worker_v2.py:83), so decode goes to `_forward_decode`. That calls `_run_target_block`, which calls `forward_batch_generation(is_verify=True)` (uno_worker_v2.py:324-328), and that returns before sampling (tp_worker.py:725-727). `run_eagle_verify` is never called, so no CanaryInfoDeviceOutput is produced. Each step commits `accepted_specs + 2` tokens (uno_worker_v2.py:407), while `canary_infos` keeps the single prefill entry. The slice at output_streamer.py:716 then yields fewer values than tokens, so `_check_canary_infos` returns a mismatch with actual=None on every chunk. In RAISE mode the RuntimeError stops handle_loop. The base branch has no INFO path. The allow-list that fixed the earlier NGRAM/DFLASH/DSpark entry is what lets UNO in.

**Verification:** Linear UNO decode calls `target_worker.forward_batch_generation(..., is_verify=True)` (uno_worker_v2.py:324-328), and tp_worker.py:725-727 returns before sampling, so `on_sampled` never fires. uno_worker_v2.py has no canary calls at all. 🔴 Diffusion-LLM servers (`--dllm-algorithm`) running with INFO get a `kv_canary_info_mismatch` on every output chunk, and in raise mode the tokenizer output loop crashes. The dLLM path never produces canary infos, and `CanaryConfig.from_env` does not reject it. Fix: when INFO is active, also assert `get_exec().dllm.dllm_algorithm is None` in from_env. That rejects every generation path that commits tokens without `on_sampled` or `on_verify_accept`, not only the spec algorithms already checked.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log or raise on a server started with --dllm-algorithm. dLLM decoding goes through tp_worker.py:608 `self.dllm_algorithm.run(self.model_runner, forward_batch, algo_states)`. +    if customized_info is None or CANARY_INFOS_KEY not in customized_info:
+        return None
+    return customized_info[CANARY_INFOS_KEY][index]

+        "sampling_params": {
+            **CANARY_INFO_SAMPLING_PARAMS[index % len(CANARY_INFO_SAMPLING_PARAMS)],

+    digest = canary_chain_initial_hash()
+    for position, token in enumerate(prompt):

+) -> list[dict]:
+    def _send(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict:
+        try:
+            resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=timeout)
+        except requests.RequestException as exc:
+            return {"status_code": -1, "error": repr(exc)}
+        try:
+            if payload.get("stream") and resp.status_code == 200:
+                chunks = [
+                    json.loads(line[6:])

+                    if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]"
+                ]
+                assert chunks, "Streaming response did not contain any output"
+                return {"status_code": resp.status_code, "json": chunks[-1]}
+            return {"status_code": resp.status_code, "json": resp.json()}
+        except ValueError:
+            return {"status_code": resp.status_code, "error": resp.text}
+
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, len(payloads))) as pool:
+        return list(pool.map(_send, payloads))

+def _random_sampler(rng: random.Random, rows: int) -> dict:
+    def f32(values: list[float]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEVICE)
+
+    return dict(
+        temperatures=f32(
+            [rng.choice([0.0, 1.0, rng.uniform(0.01, 2.0)]) for _ in range(rows)]
+        ),
+        top_ps=f32([rng.choice([1.0, rng.uniform(0.01, 1.0)]) for _ in range(rows)]),
+        top_ks=torch.tensor(
+            [
+                rng.choice([-1, 1, 1 << 30, rng.randint(-(1 << 31), (1 << 31) - 1)])
+                for _ in range(rows)
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=_DEVICE,
+        ),
+        min_ps=f32([rng.choice([0.0, rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0)]) for _ in range(rows)]),
+    )
+
+
+def _random_chain_buf(
+    rng: random.Random, num_chains: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, list[int]]:
+    buf = make_canary_buf(num_slots=_NUM_SLOTS, slot_stride_bytes=32, device=_DEVICE)
+    free_slots = list(range(1, _NUM_SLOTS))
+    rng.shuffle(free_slots)
+    last_slots: list[int] = []
+    cursor = 0
+    for _ in range(num_chains):
+        chain_len = rng.randint(1, 3)
+        if rng.random() < 0.1 or cursor + chain_len > len(free_slots):
+            last_slots.append(-1)
+            continue
+        slots = free_slots[cursor : cursor + chain_len]
+        cursor += chain_len
+        start = rng.randint(0, 4096)
+        stamp_clean_chain(
+            cuda_buf=buf,
+            ref_buf=buf,
+            slot_indices=slots,
+            tokens=[rng.randint(0, 200000) for _ in slots],
+            positions=list(range(start, start + chain_len)),
+        )
+        last_slots.append(slots[-1])
+    return buf, last_slots
+
+
+def _run_one(rng: random.Random, *, wide: bool) -> None:
+    batch_size = rng.randint(1, 128 if wide else 512)
+    width = rng.randint(1, 8) if wide else 1
+    num_tokens = batch_size * width
+    buf, last_slots = _random_chain_buf(rng, num_tokens)
+    accept_lens = (
+        torch.tensor(
+            [rng.randint(0, width) for _ in range(batch_size)],

+            device=_DEVICE,
+        )

+    )
+    slots = torch.tensor(

+    ).view(batch_size, width)
+    out_kernel, out_ref = run_canary_info_kernel_pair(
+        launch=launch_canary_info_kernel,
+        launch_ref=launch_canary_info_kernel_torch_reference,
+        out_like=torch.empty((batch_size, width), dtype=torch.int64, device=_DEVICE),
+        canary_buf=buf,
+        out_cache_loc=slots,
+        accept_lens=accept_lens,
+        next_token_ids=torch.tensor(

The dLLM path never produces canary infos, and `CanaryConfig.from_env` does not reject it. Fix: when INFO is active, also assert `get_exec().dllm.dllm_algorithm is None` in from_env. That rejects every generation path that commits tokens without `on_sampled` or `on_verify_accept`, not only the spec algorithms already checked.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log or raise on a server started with --dllm-algorithm. dLLM decoding goes through tp_worker.py:608 `self.dllm_algorithm.run(self.model_runner, forward_batch, algo_states)`. The algorithms in dllm/algorithm/base.py:119-162 call `model_runner.forward` only, never `ModelRunner.sample`, so `CanaryManager.on_sampled` never runs. `process_batch_result_dllm` (dllm/mixin/scheduler.py:119,157) extends `req.output_ids` without consuming any auxiliary output and then streams. On the tokenizer side, `_check_canary_infos` (tokenizer_manager_hook.py:100-109) sees `canary_infos` None for a non-empty chunk and returns a mismatch with actual=None. In RAISE mode the RuntimeError escapes `_handle_batch_output` and stops `handle_loop`. The checks in config.py:86-113 cover only PP, disaggregation, auto-truncate and the speculative settings, so dllm_algorithm gets through. On the base branch INFO does not exist and dLLM canary runs are unaffected.

**Verification:** Trigger: SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1 with --kv-canary log/raise on a server started with --dllm-algorithm. config.py `from_env` never checks `dllm_algorithm`. In raise mode, `raise RuntimeError(mismatch.format())` runs inside the tokenizer output handling loop. The base branch has no INFO path, so this is new.

Findings marked 🟡 are optional suggestions and need no follow-up push.

**Additional findings** (outside the current diff — GitHub can't attach inline comments there):

- 🟡 `python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/config.py` — Operators running INFO with NGRAM, DFLASH or DSpark speculation get a mismatch on every decode chunk, and in raise mode the tokenizer loop crashes. Canary infos for accepted tokens come only from `on_verify_accept`, which only `run_eagle_verify` calls. The guard at config.py:981-994 checks topk and draft-token counts for any `speculative_algorithm`, so these configs pass it. Fix: in `from_env`, accept INFO with speculation only for the algorithms whose verify goes through `run_eagle_verify` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, multi-layer EAGLE, UNO), or add the hook to every other verify path.

  <details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

  Trigger: SGLANG_KV_CANARY_ENABLE_INFO=1, kv_canary=log or raise, and a speculative algorithm such as NGRAM (ngram_worker.py:437), DFLASH (dflash_worker_v2.py:2474) or DSpark (frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py:770). These verify through `target_worker.forward_batch_generation(..., is_verify=True)` and never reach `run_eagle_verify`, so `CanaryManager.on_verify_accept` never runs. No `canary_infos` are recorded for tokens accepted in decode, only for the prefill token from `on_sampled`. In tokenizer_manager_hook.py `_check_canary_infos` sees `len(canary_infos) != len(token_ids)` or None and reports a mismatch for every chunk. In RAISE mode `on_batch_output` raises RuntimeError inside `TokenizerManager._handle_batch_output`, which takes down the handle loop for all requests. The guard in `CanaryConfig.from_env` only asserts `speculative_eagle_topk == 1` and `speculative_num_draft_tokens == speculative_num_steps + 1`. It does not check which algorithm is in use, so these setups get past it.

  **Verification:** The only place accepted spec tokens get canary infos is `CanaryManager.on_verify_accept`, and it is called only from `run_eagle_verify` (eagle_worker_common.py:684 and :833). The guard is config.py:84-97, not :981-994. So every decode chunk that carries spec-accepted tokens is reported as a mismatch, and in raise mode the tokenizer loop gets an exception.

  </details>
